title: Trump 'Deep State' Purge Promise Stayed In Progress on AP Dashboard
description_short: Trump 'Deep State' Purge Promise Stayed In Progress on AP Dashboard
description_medium: AP’s tracker showed Trump’s pledge to uproot what he calls the “deep state” as “in progress” on Feb. 28, 2026. That label describes the tracker’s assessment at that time; it does not establish that a particular official or agency had been removed or changed. AP separately reported growing frustration among some Trump supporters over the pledge’s progress, leaving its implementation unsettled.
description_long: As of Feb. 28, 2026, the Associated Press campaign-promise tracker listed Donald Trump’s pledge to uproot what he calls the “deep state” as in progress. The status is AP’s assessment of the pledge, not an official report of completed personnel changes or a finding that any agency had changed its practices. AP’s related reporting described frustration among some Trump supporters about the pace of progress on such promises, showing that the pledge remained politically salient. The linked material does not specify which employees, offices, or policies count toward fulfillment, and it does not quantify effects on the civil service. The entry therefore records the tracker’s dated status and the continuing public dispute over the promise, while leaving its practical scope and outcome open. Readers should distinguish the political phrase “deep state” from a defined government program: the tracker label alone does not show what actions would satisfy the pledge or whether those actions had occurred by the date shown.

preserved_fields.title: Trump 'Deep State' Purge Promise Stayed In Progress on AP Dashboard
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump 'Deep State' Purge Promise Stayed In Progress on AP Dashboard

notes: AP’s tracker page displays the status assessment; the linked AP coverage provides broader political context but does not specify the pledge’s implementation or measurable effects.

title: State Legislature Election Override Authorization - Independent State Legislature Theory Implementation
description_short: State Legislature Election Override Authorization - Independent State Legislature Theory Implementation
description_medium: After Joe Biden’s certified 2020 victory, Donald Trump pressed Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp to call a special legislative session and urged officials in other states to consider replacing the voters’ choice of electors. Brookings explains that the then-existing Electoral Count Act contained a narrow “failed to make a choice” provision that became part of this pressure campaign. Congress later enacted the Electoral Count Reform Act to close that provision.
description_long: In the weeks after the 2020 election, Donald Trump sought to have state legislatures intervene in the certified results. On Dec. 5, 2020, he urged Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp to call a special session; the supplied account also describes pressure directed at officials in Pennsylvania and Michigan. Brookings explains the legal argument behind the effort: a provision in the then-existing Electoral Count Act allowed a legislature to name electors after Election Day if it determined that voters had “failed” to make a choice. The article describes this as a narrow loophole and says Trump’s effort brought it into focus. It does not mean state legislatures generally had authority to disregard certified election results. Congress later passed the bipartisan Electoral Count Reform Act, which closed the “failed choice” provision and clarified the process for counting electoral votes. This episode shows how the campaign sought to use an unresolved statutory exception after voters had chosen electors. The linked sources support the pressure campaign and the law’s subsequent repair; they do not establish that the theory gave state lawmakers a lawful basis to overturn the result.

preserved_fields.title: State Legislature Election Override Authorization - Independent State Legislature Theory Implementation
preserved_fields.description_short: State Legislature Election Override Authorization - Independent State Legislature Theory Implementation

notes: The existing category was noncanonical and has been changed to Election Interference. Brookings is an opinion analysis; its description of the former statutory loophole is kept distinct from the settled rule and the later Electoral Count Reform Act.

title: Trump's Epstein Accountability Exposure Grew as DOJ Webpage Removals Became Public
description_short: Trump's Epstein Accountability Exposure Grew as DOJ Webpage Removals Became Public
description_medium: The AP reported that at least 16 files disappeared from the Justice Department’s public Epstein-documents webpage less than a day after release. One missing image included photographs of Donald Trump, Jeffrey Epstein, Melania Trump, and Ghislaine Maxwell. The department had not publicly explained the removals when AP reported them on Dec. 20, 2025.
description_long: On Dec. 20, 2025, the Associated Press reported that at least 16 files had disappeared from the Justice Department’s public webpage for documents related to Jeffrey Epstein. The files had been available the previous day. Among them was an image showing a drawer with several photographs, including Donald Trump, Epstein, Melania Trump, and Ghislaine Maxwell. AP said the department had removed the files without explanation or public notice at the time of publication. The report documents a change to the public records page and identifies the image’s contents; it does not establish why the files were removed, whether the department later restored them, or whether the removal was intended to hide information about Trump. Those unanswered questions matter because the subject was an official document release involving a high-profile criminal case, but the reporting does not prove selective handling or political motive. The event is therefore the unexplained disappearance of records from the DOJ page, including one image in which Trump appeared alongside Epstein and others—not a finding about what that photograph shows beyond the people visible in it.

preserved_fields.title: Trump's Epstein Accountability Exposure Grew as DOJ Webpage Removals Became Public
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump's Epstein Accountability Exposure Grew as DOJ Webpage Removals Became Public

notes: Retitled to describe AP’s documented finding; the report did not establish motive for the removals or a connection between the missing files and wrongdoing by Trump.

title: Trump's Tariff Refund Delay Bid Failed, Accelerating Financial Consequences
description_short: Trump's Tariff Refund Delay Bid Failed, Accelerating Financial Consequences
description_medium: A federal appeals court rejected the Trump administration’s request to pause tariff-refund proceedings for 90 days. The court sent the next stage to the U.S. Court of International Trade to work out the process after the Supreme Court ruled the tariffs illegal. The decision removed the requested delay, but did not itself determine each importer’s refund.
description_long: On March 2, 2026, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit rejected the Trump administration’s request to hold tariff-refund proceedings for 90 days. The administration had asked the appeals court to proceed cautiously while the next phase was addressed. Instead, the court sent the matter to the U.S. Court of International Trade to sort out the refund process. The dispute followed the Supreme Court’s Feb. 20 ruling that Trump’s sweeping tariffs on most countries were illegal. The ruling removed the delay the Justice Department had requested and moved the refund question to the lower court. It did not itself set the amount owed to any importer, establish a payment timetable, or resolve every claim. The linked AP report describes a procedural development in the aftermath of the tariff decision, rather than a completed round of payments. The administration’s broader trade policy therefore faced a judicial limit, while the practical financial consequences depended on further proceedings. The reporting supports the court actions and dates; it does not quantify the final refunds or their effect on federal finances.

preserved_fields.title: Trump's Tariff Refund Delay Bid Failed, Accelerating Financial Consequences
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump's Tariff Refund Delay Bid Failed, Accelerating Financial Consequences

notes: Descriptions distinguish rejection of the requested 90-day pause from the unresolved refund process and any eventual payment.

title: NPR Review Finds Missing Pages and Redaction Errors in Epstein Files Release
description_short: NPR Review Finds Missing Pages and Redaction Errors in Epstein Files Release
description_medium: NPR reported that its review of Epstein-file numbers found 53 pages of interview documents and notes apparently missing from the public database. It also described thousands of pages the Justice Department removed and reuploaded to correct redactions that had exposed victim names. The reporting identifies a records dispute and privacy failures, but does not measure any change in Trump’s credibility.
description_long: NPR’s February 24, 2026, examination focused on gaps and corrections in the Justice Department’s Epstein-files release. Comparing three sets of serial numbers, the outlet identified 53 pages of interview documents and notes that appeared to be missing from the public database. NPR separately reported that the department had removed and reuploaded thousands of pages in recent weeks to fix improperly redacted victim names. The report included criticism from an attorney for a witness in Ghislaine Maxwell’s trial, who said the release exposed people who had fought to remain anonymous. It also described the Justice Department’s position that records were not withheld or redacted because of embarrassment, reputational harm, or political sensitivity, along with a White House defense of Trump. These competing statements make the completeness and handling of the files the documented issue. NPR’s reporting does not establish a change in public opinion, a measurable loss of credibility, or that the file irregularities proved allegations against Trump. Those broader reputation claims remain interpretation rather than an outcome shown by the documents.

title: Trump's Promise Messaging Chose Certainty Even as PBS Framed Mixed Outcomes
description_short: Trump's Promise Messaging Chose Certainty Even as PBS Framed Mixed Outcomes
description_medium: During a January 2026 speech in Detroit, Trump said he had kept all his campaign promises. A PolitiFact review carried by PBS compared that claim with its tracker of 75 second-term promises: about 19% were rated kept, while roughly 45% were in the works and 31% stalled. The tracker evaluates measurable outcomes, not effort or intent.
description_long: In a January 2026 Detroit speech, Donald Trump said he had kept all his campaign promises and cited policies including taxes on tips and Social Security, tariffs, and environmental regulation. A Feb. 23 review by PolitiFact, published by PBS, compared the claim with its tracker of 75 promises from Trump’s second-term campaign. The review rated about 19% as kept, approximately 45% as in the works, and about 31% as stalled; several tax promises were rated compromises. PolitiFact says it evaluates measurable outcomes rather than intentions or efforts. Its examples included the promise to end taxes on Social Security, which the 2025 tax law addressed only partially, and the promise to end the war in Ukraine within 24 hours, which remained unfulfilled in the review. The comparison shows a gap between Trump’s blanket statement and the tracker’s mixed ratings. It does not imply that every promise was broken: some were fulfilled, some partially addressed, and others remained unfinished. The entry concerns the accuracy of the broad “all promises kept” claim against the contemporaneous tracker, not a judgment about whether the underlying promises were desirable.

preserved_fields.title: Trump's Promise Messaging Chose Certainty Even as PBS Framed Mixed Outcomes
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump's Promise Messaging Chose Certainty Even as PBS Framed Mixed Outcomes

notes: PolitiFact’s tracker is a progress assessment based on measurable outcomes; percentages and examples are attributed to its Feb. 23, 2026 review.

title: Trump's Early Rights Shock Continued to Imply Long-Horizon Repair Costs
description_short: Trump's Early Rights Shock Continued to Imply Long-Horizon Repair Costs
description_medium: Amnesty International’s April 30, 2025 review of Trump’s first 100 days described actions affecting asylum, protest, press freedom, and the rule of law, including the detention of Columbia student Mahmoud Khalil. The organization argued that overlapping policies could weaken rights protections. Its report presents an advocacy assessment; it does not quantify the duration or cost of later institutional repair.
description_long: On April 30, 2025, Amnesty International published a review of human-rights issues during Donald Trump’s first 100 days back in office. The organization cited restrictions on asylum, deportation threats against noncitizen student protesters, actions affecting press freedom, and disputes over compliance with court orders. It highlighted Mahmoud Khalil, a Palestinian student and lawful permanent resident detained and placed in deportation proceedings after participating in protests at Columbia University. Amnesty also described foreign-aid cuts and withdrawals from international bodies as part of the same period. The report is an advocacy organization’s assessment of policies and their human-rights implications, not a court ruling on every action it discusses. Its account provides examples of the rights and institutions at issue, but it does not calculate how long any resulting legal or institutional repair would take or what it would cost. The entry’s “long-horizon repair costs” framing should therefore be read as an implication rather than a measured outcome. The documented event is Amnesty’s assessment and the policies it identifies, including the Khalil case, not a quantified estimate of future repair burdens.

preserved_fields.title: Trump's Early Rights Shock Continued to Imply Long-Horizon Repair Costs
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump's Early Rights Shock Continued to Imply Long-Horizon Repair Costs

notes: Descriptions attribute broad conclusions to Amnesty and separate its assessment from judicial findings and unmeasured future repair costs.

title: AP Described Trump’s Shifting and Conflicting Statements on Iran
description_short: AP Described Trump’s Shifting and Conflicting Statements on Iran
description_medium: The AP compared Trump’s statements about Iran before and after military strikes. After earlier attacks, he and his administration said Iran’s nuclear program had been obliterated; before later U.S.-Israeli strikes, they warned more urgently about Iran’s nuclear ambitions. AP also described threats during January protests that Trump later stepped back from.
description_long: An Associated Press report published March 2, 2026, examined how Donald Trump and his administration described Iran’s nuclear program and the possibility of further military action. After strikes the previous summer, officials repeatedly said the attacks had obliterated the program and set back Iran’s ability to build a nuclear weapon for years. In the lead-up to later U.S.-Israeli strikes, Trump and administration officials issued more urgent warnings about Iran’s nuclear ambitions. AP also recounted Trump’s January threats of military action amid protests in Iran, followed by a decision to step back after he said he had been assured Tehran had stopped killing protesters and had not carried out a planned execution. The report presents a record of changing public statements, not an independent technical assessment of Iran’s nuclear capacity or a finding about what allied governments did in response. The entry’s earlier claim that these signals taxed allied planning was not substantiated by the supplied source, so the title and descriptions focus on the documented statements and their sequence.

preserved_fields.title: Trump's Conflicting Iran Signals Continued to Tax Allied Planning
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump's Conflicting Iran Signals Continued to Tax Allied Planning

notes: Retitled to remove the unsupported claim about allied planning; AP supports the sequence of public statements but is not an independent assessment of Iran’s nuclear program.
